title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 35
paragraphs: While Croesus was busy with his son’s marriage, there came to Sardis a man under a misfortune, with unclean hands—a Phrygian by birth and of the royal house. This man came to the house of Croesus and, according to the customs that prevail in that land, asked that he might be purified. Croesus granted him the purification, for the manner of purification among the Lydians is almost the same as what the Greeks use. So when Croesus had performed what was customary, he asked the stranger where he came from and who he was, saying: “Man, who are you, and from what part of Phrygia have you come to sit upon my hearth? And what man or woman have you killed?” He answered: “O king, I am the son of Gordias, son of Midas, and I am called Adrastus. I killed my own brother against my will, and for this reason I am here, having been driven out by my father and stripped of all that I had.” Croesus answered him: “You are, as it happens, the offshoot of men who are our friends, and you have come among friends, where you shall want for nothing as long as you remain in our land. And you will find it most to your profit to bear this misfortune as lightly as you can.” So the man made his home with Croesus.
